record_notes.DCP-LETT-1103: July 21, supplied 1847, copy. Missed Denny at Oxford, permits retention of duplicates and conditionally specimens independently known in British Museum. Lyell procured lice but their forwarding to Denny is only possible, enquiry planned for autumn. Earlier Denny parasite letter 785 does not supply current note. Copyist A. Denny differs from identified Henry; preserve literal with separate correction. Historical racial wording retained as source attribution, not modern gloss.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1059: February 9, supplied 1847, answers missing January 5 Dieffenbach letter after lending it to Lyell and receiving it back only days earlier. Darwin had read it before loan and wished to reread; no precise original receipt. Bunsen views and observations reported through Dieffenbach, Palagonite/Pelagonite equivalence suspected not established. Lyell volcanic chapters already printed, wished citation is counterfactual. Von Dechen copy not received as reported; safe dispatch assurances do not prove arrival, Dieffenbach own receipt only hoped. Tschudi ordered, later March 8 reading not backdated. Variation-note work planned about a year ahead but later actual 1854 commencement separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1343A: July 14, supplied 1850 from August box account. Prior enquiry about a week ago perhaps misaddressed Burch instead of Downie; no reply, dimensions/prices still requested. Raw existing-box dimensions are 16 by 12¼ inches, 4 inches deep, not 1214. Larger plain deal box desired, no lock/key. Later payment for Willy box is future outcome, not completed order here. Recipient inferred from address book and two-name labels.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2305: Fresh reading of previously accepted boundary copy: Friday in disjoint 1845–1847 or 1857–1864 ranges, with even 1843 possibility acknowledged in date rationale. No specific meeting or day identified from head symptoms. Raw mixed number is 2½, a proposed visit time, not 212 or a date. Prefers going to Falconer so can leave if ill; nonarrival would indicate illness, not actual cancellation. Later symptom records do not select one date. Retain prior period/late-cutoff holds.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1135: November 13, 1847 explicit. Thanks a newer missing Grey letter offering forgiveness and natural-history help; not the preserved May 10, 1846 return of leaked letter 979. Proposes New Zealand cave excavation and erratic-boulder investigation, reports past inability to enter burial caves, asks glacial-age evidence rather than supplying observations not yet made. Colonial value judgments and till/iceberg theory are historical author views. Burn-letter sentence is historical suggestion to recipient, not agent instruction. Author Sir Grey before actual 1848 knighthood is retained discrepancy, not reason to redateline.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1166A: March 28, supplied 1848, Admiralty manuscript search. Missing Herschel message says parcel not received or mislaid, Darwin strongly believes Admiralty has it but no proof. His tentative March 15 posting belief conflicts with independently accepted March 21 enclosure letter and March 20 completion; preserve belief and correction separately. Full 50-page manuscript unavailable. Raw addressee R A B Hamilton versus identified W A B Hamilton remains explicit. Search asked, possible Auckland involvement conjecture; footnote March 23 Herschel instruction/stamp March 28 are not full incoming text or proved Darwin receipt. May registered resend is later.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1344: August 6, supplied 1850. Missing Harris note of August 2 known, fossils classified this morning and numbered; many valves unnamed because condition or nondiagnostic anatomy. Numbered list skips 4, repeats 7 to across blocks and includes do, alternatives and question marks; raw paragraphs not a table. New forms partly too immature to name, generic assignment tentative. Original chalk beds unknown, broad upper-chalk affinity only inference. More specimens requested by August 18, return and describing planned for 18/19; later journal records actual return August 16, not current knowledge or correction of intention.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1078: Only an editorial synopsis of a ten-page algae memorandum is transcribed; no Darwin wording survives on this page. Underlying Beagle diary notes and missing specimens are described but not reproduced. Published Harvey account or Darwin Coral reefs cannot substitute for full memorandum. Record fully inspected, authentic body unavailable.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13869: Copy testimonial to Hawkins, 1848–1851 range inferred from other testimonials and office/life dates. Date crosses current period; other letters in collected file do not assign an exact writing day. Shared praise with 679 is not a new incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1201: Only Sotheby catalogue synopsis, no quoted Darwin words, of October 5, 1848 Baily barnacle note. Recipient identified by catalogue. It describes request to send specimens to Geological Society, not actual arrival or available incoming wording. Entire paragraph is editorial narration and cannot train Darwin voice. Authentic letter body unavailable.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1040: Sunday within 1847 watermark to November 12, 1848 editorial interval, bounded by father death on following day. Next morning after Geological Society meeting heard father had sought introduction via old friend, so releases Hutton from further effort. Father friend intimacy with Lady Finch probable, her identity likely but not certain. Actual prior meeting and father message missing. Death-based latest bound is editorial inference, not literal dateline; do not equate meeting, news, introduction and composition days.
